title:
From sunshine
to switched-on.
eyebrow: EVERYDAY SCIENCE / AN ILLUSTRATED FIELD NOTE
subtitle: How a solar panel turns a little sunlight into useful electricity.
headerNote:
A little physics.
A lot of possibility.

chapters.title: Meet the sunlight
chapters.explanation: Sunlight carries energy as photons. A photovoltaic cell can absorb some of that energy; it does not need the panel to become hot.

chapters.title: Capture the energy
chapters.explanation: Absorbed light energy creates mobile electrical charges in the photovoltaic material. An internal electrical field separates charges, and a connected circuit carries direct current (DC).

chapters.title: Make it home-ready
chapters.explanation: An inverter changes the panel's DC electricity into alternating current (AC), the form supplied to a typical household electrical system. A system may use a shared inverter or panel-level microinverters.

chapters.title: Put it to work
chapters.explanation: AC electricity can supply household loads. This simplified drawing shows the direct daytime path. A real installation also includes wiring, protection and metering; batteries can store energy and a grid connection can supply shortfalls or receive surplus where supported.

captions.text: Let's follow sunlight on its way to a useful job.
Sunlight carries energy in tiny packets called photons.
Photovoltaic cells turn absorbed light energy into DC electricity.
The inverter changes direct current, DC, into alternating current, AC.
That AC electricity can supply a home's lights and appliances.
Panel: capture. Inverter: convert. Home: use. That's the daytime path.
